<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
Herod the Great was a king of Judea, also known as the Herodian kingdom, who ruled from 37 BCE to 4 BCE. He was the son of Antipater the Idumaean, a high-ranking official under the Hasmonean dynasty, and was appointed king by the Roman Senate. Herod is best known for his ambitious building projects, including the renovation of the Second Temple in Jerusalem and the construction of the port city of Caesarea Maritima. He was also known for his ruthless tactics, including the slaughter of the innocents, a mass killing of male children in Bethlehem and the surrounding areas in an attempt to kill the newborn Jesus, according to the New Testament. Despite his controversial reign, Herod is considered one of the greatest rulers in Jewish history for his military victories, administrative skills, and cultural achievements.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->

Antipater was an Edomite, a member of a group of people who lived in the region of Edom, which is located in modern-day southern Jordan and northern Saudi Arabia. The Edomites were descendants of Esau, the brother of Jacob (also known as Israel) in the Hebrew Bible. Despite his Edomite origins, Herod was appointed king of Judea by the Roman Senate and is considered one of the greatest rulers in Jewish history.

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_005_BEGIN -->
Herod the Great became king of Judea, also known as the Herodian kingdom, in 37 BCE after the Roman Senate appointed him to the position. At the time, Judea was a client state of the Roman Empire, and the Roman Senate had the authority to appoint the ruler of Judea.

Before becoming king, Herod served as an official under the Hasmonean dynasty, a Jewish dynasty that ruled Judea. He gained the favor of the Roman Senate and the Roman general Marcus Licinius Crassus, who supported his bid for the throne. When the last Hasmonean ruler, Antigonus II Mattathias, was defeated by the Romans, Herod was appointed king by the Roman Senate.

Despite his Edomite origins, Herod was accepted by the Jewish people as their ruler and is considered one of the greatest rulers in Jewish history for his military victories, administrative skills, and cultural achievements.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_005_END -->
